description: Learn how to crop an image in Photoshop on Mac: press C, drag the border, set ratios, apply with Return, and undo safely in Photoshop 2026.

intro: To crop an image in Photoshop on Mac, press C to select the Crop tool, then drag a corner handle or draw a new border inside the image. Press Return, click the checkmark in the Options Bar, or double-click inside the border to apply the crop.
tldr: Press C to pick the Crop tool, then drag a corner handle or draw a new border.
Hold Shift to lock proportions, or Option to resize from the center.
Press Return, click the checkmark, or double-click inside the border to apply.
Delete Cropped Pixels is on by default. Turn it off if you may need the cut-off edges later.
Undo with ⌘Z or Edit > Undo Crop while the file is still open.

blocks.text: Before you crop: save a copy first

Cropping feels harmless, but in Photoshop it can remove pixels for good. Before you touch the Crop tool, decide whether the original must stay whole. If it must, save a copy first. Choose File > Save As and give the copy a new name. Then crop the copy, so the original is still there if the framing turns out too tight.
Pick the Crop tool and draw a border

Press C to select the Crop tool, or click it in the toolbar. The image gets a border with handles on each edge and corner. Drag a corner handle inward to trim two sides at once. Drag an edge handle to trim one side. Drag outside the image if you want to draw a fresh border from nothing.

Edge handles suit a problem on one side only, such as a stray object at the edge of the frame. Corner handles are faster when the whole composition needs tightening. You can use both in the same crop.
Keep proportions with Shift and Option

Hold Shift while you drag a corner to lock the proportions. The border keeps its shape as it shrinks or grows. Hold Option to resize from the center instead of the opposite corner. Hold Shift and Option together to lock proportions and keep the crop centered on the image.

blocks.text: Locking proportions matters when a print frame or a web slot has a fixed shape. It also helps when you crop a set of photos that must match. For an exact number, skip the dragging and type values in the Options Bar, as covered below.
Set exact sizes and ratios in the Options Bar

The Options Bar runs across the top of the Photoshop window while the Crop tool is active. Open the Aspect Ratio menu to choose a preset. You can also type your own width, height, and resolution into the boxes. Click the Swap icon to flip width and height in one click. Reset returns the border to the full image.

The Aspect Ratio menu also lists W x H x Resolution, New Crop Preset, and Clear. Use New Crop Preset to save a shape you use often, such as a banner size for a website. Clear removes the ratio so you can drag freely again.

Two more controls help with framing. Press O to cycle the overlay guides, which help you place the subject. Use Straighten to rotate the image when a horizon or a wall leans. Both sit in the Options Bar, so you do not need to open another panel.
Apply the crop or cancel it
A crop does not apply until you commit it. Press Return, click the checkmark in the Options Bar, or double-click inside the border. Any of the three works. Pick the one that suits your hands.
To leave without cropping, click Cancel in the Options Bar. The image goes back to its full size, and nothing is removed. Cancel is the safe choice when you are not sure about the border.
Delete Cropped Pixels: the setting that matters most

Delete Cropped Pixels is the checkbox that matters most. It is on by default. When it is on, Photoshop permanently deletes the cropped pixels once you apply the crop. You cannot bring those edges back from the file later.
This can surprise you later. If you enlarge the border past the edge of the original image, the empty areas fill with the Background color. It shows up when you extend a crop to make room for text.

When you turn the checkbox off, Photoshop hides the cropped pixels instead. They stay in the file, and Image > Reveal All brings them back. This is the safer setting for a working file, because you can change your mind later.

items: Leave it on for a final file you will never crop again.
Turn it off for a working file or any crop you might change.
Save a copy before any crop you want to keep reversible.

blocks.text: Undo a crop or recover cut-off pixels

Undo works as long as the file is still open. Press ⌘Z right after you apply the crop, or choose Edit > Undo Crop from the menu bar. Either one reverses the crop. Once you close the file, that undo is no longer available.

If Delete Cropped Pixels was off, go to Image > Reveal All. The hidden pixels return, and you can adjust the framing again. This works only while the hidden pixels are still in the file. If you have saved over the file since then, keep your copy as the fallback.
Crop and extend the canvas with Generative Expand

Generative Expand turns the Crop tool into an extender. You drag an edge outward past the image, and Photoshop fills the new area with AI-generated pixels. PhotoshopNews describes this as AI outpainting through the Crop Tool. It helps when you need room for a headline or a wider frame.

To use it, change Transparent to Generative Expand in the Crop tool options bar. Drag the edge of the crop outward. Press the checkmark or Enter to apply it. The Firefly Fill and Expand model, released in January 2026, works at 2k for most cases. That is 2024 x 2024 px, up from the earlier 1k limit.
Generative Expand creates new content, so check the extended areas closely. Look at edges, hands, and any text. Keep your untouched copy so you can try again with different settings.
Common mistakes when cropping in Photoshop on Mac

items: Cropping the only copy of a file while Delete Cropped Pixels is on.
Dragging a handle and assuming the crop applied. It applies only after you commit.
Dragging an edge handle and expecting proportions to stay locked. Use a corner handle with Shift for that.
Using old tool settings. Control-click the Crop tool icon in the Options Bar and choose Reset Tool.
Expecting the border to reset with the tool. Resetting the tool does not reset the border. Switch tools, then select Crop again.

blocks.text: Crop for print, web, and social posts

For print, the shape usually comes from the frame or the printer. Lock the proportions first. Then set the exact size in the Options Bar. Keep faces and key details away from the edges, so a frame does not cut into them.

For web and social posts, the shape matters more than anything else. Pick a preset from the Aspect Ratio menu for the slot you need. Then press O to cycle the overlay guides until the subject sits where you want it.
Which Photoshop version this guide covers

Photoshop 2026 is version 27. Adobe released version 27.0 in October 2025, tied to Adobe MAX. The newest release in this research is version 27.5, released April 1, 2026. Newer builds may exist, so check your own number with Photoshop > About Photoshop.

The crop steps here come from Photoshop Essentials. That guide was written for Photoshop 2021 and says it works with recent versions. For version details, see [how to check your Photoshop version on Mac](/how-to/check-your-photoshop-version-in-photoshop).

blocks.title: Labels can differ
blocks.text: Menu names and button labels can change between Photoshop releases. Check the Options Bar on your own screen before you rely on a specific label.

faq.question: What is the keyboard shortcut to crop an image in Photoshop on Mac?
faq.answer: Press C to select the Crop tool. Drag the border, then press Return to apply it. Press ⌘Z right after to undo the crop.

faq.question: How do I crop to an exact size or shape?
faq.answer: Open the Aspect Ratio menu in the Options Bar and pick a preset. For an exact size, type values into the Width and Height boxes. Click the Swap icon to flip the shape.

faq.question: Why did my cropped pixels disappear?
faq.answer: Delete Cropped Pixels was probably on. It is on by default, and it permanently removes cropped pixels. Turn it off before you crop if you may need them later.

faq.question: Can I get the cropped pixels back?
faq.answer: Yes, if Delete Cropped Pixels was off. Use Image > Reveal All. If it was on, the pixels are deleted, so only an earlier copy of the file can help.

faq.question: Can Photoshop extend the canvas while I crop?
faq.answer: Yes. Use Generative Expand from the Crop tool. Change Transparent to Generative Expand, drag an edge outward, then press the checkmark or Enter.

faq.question: Do these steps work in Photoshop on the web?
faq.answer: This guide covers the desktop app on a Mac. Check Adobe's help pages for the web version, since its menus can differ.

faq.question: Which Photoshop version do I need?
faq.answer: These steps target Photoshop 2026, which is version 27. The newest release confirmed here is version 27.5, released April 1, 2026. Check your version with Photoshop > About Photoshop.

task: Crop a photo in Photoshop on Mac
requirements: The image file you want to crop
A copy of the file if you may need the original later
About five minutes for a first crop

steps.name: Open the image
steps.text: Press ⌘O or choose File > Open, then pick your photo and click Open. If the photo is already open, click its tab or window instead.
steps.tip: Work on a copy when the crop might need to be undone later.

steps.name: Select the Crop tool
steps.text: Press C, or click the Crop tool in the toolbar. A border appears with handles on each edge and corner. The Options Bar at the top changes to show crop settings.
steps.tip: If C does nothing, click the image first so Photoshop is listening to the keyboard.

steps.name: Drag a handle or draw a new border
steps.text: Drag a corner handle inward to trim two sides at once. Drag an edge handle to trim one side. To start a fresh border, drag outside the image.
steps.tip: Hold Shift while dragging a corner to keep the current proportions.

steps.name: Resize from the center
steps.text: Hold Option while dragging a handle to resize from the center. Hold Shift and Option together to lock proportions and keep the crop centered.

steps.name: Set a ratio or exact size
steps.text: Open the Aspect Ratio menu in the Options Bar to choose a preset. Or type a width and height in the boxes. Click the Swap icon to flip width and height.
steps.tip: Press O to cycle the overlay guides and place your subject.

steps.name: Check Delete Cropped Pixels
steps.text: Find the Delete Cropped Pixels checkbox in the Options Bar. It is on by default, which permanently removes the cropped pixels. Turn it off if you may need them later.
steps.tip: With the box off, use Image > Reveal All to bring the cut-off pixels back.

steps.name: Apply the crop
steps.text: Press Return, click the checkmark in the Options Bar, or double-click inside the border. The canvas shrinks to the new border.

steps.name: Undo or cancel
steps.text: Before you apply, click Cancel in the Options Bar. After you apply, press ⌘Z or choose Edit > Undo Crop.

steps.name: Save the result
steps.text: Choose File > Save As, give the cropped file a new name, and save. A separate file protects the original if the crop needs changing.

troubleshooting.fix: Press Return, click the checkmark in the Options Bar, or double-click inside the border. The crop stays pending until one of these actions runs.

troubleshooting.problem: An empty area appears when I enlarge the border
troubleshooting.fix: Delete Cropped Pixels is on, so the empty area fills with the Background color. Press ⌘Z to undo, turn the checkbox off, then crop again.
Control-click the Crop tool icon in the Options Bar and choose Reset Tool. This does not reset the border, so switch to another tool and select Crop again.

troubleshooting.problem: Layers look zoomed in after cropping
troubleshooting.fix: Adobe's August 2026 beta release notes list a fix for Relight layers that turned into a zoomed-in crop after using the Crop tool. Check that your build includes the fix, or update Photoshop.

troubleshooting.problem: I need the cut-off pixels back
troubleshooting.fix: Use Image > Reveal All if Delete Cropped Pixels was off. If it was on, the pixels are gone from the file, so reopen your saved copy or original.
